html:
The Philippine Revolution began in August 1896, when the secret society Katipunan, led by Andrés Bonifacio, rose against Spanish rule around Manila. It is counted as the first nationalist revolution in Asia.

The Katipunan was inspired by the reformers of the Propaganda Movement. Spain executed José Rizal in December 1896. Rivalry split the rebels, and Emilio Aguinaldo's faction had Bonifacio executed in 1897.

A truce sent Aguinaldo into exile, but he returned after the Battle of Manila Bay and declared independence at Kawit on 12 June 1898, now Independence Day. The Malolos Constitution followed, but the United States claimed the islands. See war with the United States.
